observations: A large solar panel assembly with multiple cells.
The panel is mounted on a white frame or support structure.
A watermark 'NAGOTECH SOLAR' is visible across the center of the image.
The image appears to be a low-resolution photo taken in a warehouse or outdoor storage area.
No brand name, model number, or technical specification plate is visible on the panel itself.

claims.evidence: No wattage label or specification plate is visible in the photo.
The cell count cannot be confirmed from the photo; it requires a clear view of the junction box or specification plate.
Origin and import status cannot be verified from a photo.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The panel may be a generic brand or a lower-wattage counterfeit.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification label or sticker on the back of the panel.

risks.risk: The panel may be physically damaged or have internal cell defects.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter test of the open-circuit voltage (Voc) and short-circuit current (Isc) in direct sunlight.

risks.risk: The frame or mounting hardware may be damaged or incomplete.
risks.proof: A photo of the full assembly with the frame and all mounting brackets clearly visible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as missing frame or hardware

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the specification label on the back of the panel showing wattage and cell count.
Video of a multimeter test showing the output voltage and current.
Photo of the full panel assembly including the frame and mounting hardware.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
